review.tagline: Drives real Android phones from natural language via CLI, web console, SDK or MCP
review.summary: ARTEMIS runs a multimodal agent that operates an Android device or emulator over ADB from plain-language instructions. It ships an MCP server for IDEs such as Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Windsurf, plus a CLI, a web console on port 8000 and a Python client. Two profiles exist: Flash, a reactive loop at about 3–5s per step, and Pro, a planner/operator/checker graph at about 15–40s per step.
review.audience: Mobile QA and Android developers wiring real devices into coding agents or CI
strengths: Native MCP server with install commands for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf and others
Flash and Pro profiles trade speed against planning and checkpoint verification
Falls back from accessibility tree to OCR and visual locating for Compose and Flutter UIs
Python client with no runtime dependencies for pytest or CI use
weaknesses: Android only; iOS support is a roadmap item
Installs an accessibility helper app on the phone at first task
Flash profile has no task plan, safety net, final report or ADB shell
Needs an external multimodal model; hardware and cost requirements are unknown
needs: Needs ADB, scrcpy, FFmpeg, uv, Python 3.12+, Android device or emulator with USB debugging
